description:
Judge a screenshot of the running UI. **Paid.**

You drive the browser; verifAIed judges what you got. Take a
screenshot of the change you just made, say what it was supposed to
do, and this returns a verdict — plus records it, so ``check_done``
can hold the branch to it.

Two modes:

- With ``intent`` (recommended): checks one claim. "The error state now
  shows a Retry button" → ``pass`` / ``fail`` / ``unclear``, with a
  confidence and the reasoning. ``unclear`` is a real answer, used when
  the screenshot doesn't show the region the claim is about — treat it
  as "screenshot the right thing and ask again", not as a pass.
- Without ``intent``: a rubric review (layout, hierarchy, legibility,
  consistency, obvious broken state) returning ``clean`` or ``issues``
  with a defect list.

``target`` attaches the verdict to one component as
``path/to/File.tsx::ComponentName``, which is what clears that
component's ``visually_unreviewed`` gap. A target that doesn't resolve
is not an error: the verdict is still recorded against the branch and
the response carries a ``warning`` saying so.

``screenshot_base64`` is the raw image bytes, base64-encoded (a
``data:`` URL prefix is fine). PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP; a viewport-sized
capture is plenty and anything over ~1.5MB of base64 is rejected with a
resize hint. Pass ``console_errors`` when you have them — a visual
defect and a console error are very often the same bug.

The screenshot **is stored** as session evidence: each call opens a
one-moment session in the branch's ledger and attaches the image to it,
so the Tests page can show the frame the verdict was about. The
reasoning text is still the record — the picture is the receipt.

Failing an intent check creates an ``intent_mismatch`` gap; a changed
component with no verdict creates ``visually_unreviewed``. Both
activate only once this branch has at least one verdict, so a repo that
doesn't use this tool never sees them.
name: verify_ui
